newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Prices firmer on buying interest.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Prices firmer on buying interest.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market was quoted higher on Thursday as low prices on late Wednesday triggered buying interest, traders said.
On Thursday afternnon, a 380-cst cargo for loading February 22-26 was traded at $90 per tonne.
"When prices fell to $93 per tonne yesterday, good buying interest emerged because it was a cheap price," said a major, adding that bids had gone up to $96-$97 late Wednesday,
"But there has been no change in fundamentals anyway and $100 should be a strong resistance," said another trader.
South Korea was expected to export two more cargoes for loading in February and Kuwait was heard to have an end-March delivery cargo for sale.

Traders said the price differential beween 180-cst and 380-cst grades have narrowed on Singapore published quotes. This triggered some concerns amongst traders who were bringing in 380-cst supplies from the Mideast.
"These traders would like to see lower 380cst quotes," said one trader.

Sentiment was largely bearish ahead the Lunar New Year holiday over the weekend though there were some anticipation that China, which has covered its demand throughout February, might enter the market in March, traders said.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
